transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Thank you. Well, I suppose what brings me in is... I keep hearing these very clear voices in my apartment. And sometimes when I'm walking through empty museum rooms, too. It sounds like women whispering right from behind the walls, telling me exactly which photographs belong in the archive. It's very specific. 

I’ve always had an eye for photography, actually. Back when I was finishing my bachelor's degree, we had to spend hours and hours in the darkroom. The smell of those developing chemicals, it really gets right into your clothes and your hair. I had this lovely wool sweater that smelled like fixer for years. Do you knit? I tried to pick it up last winter because the heating in my building is just dreadful. The radiator clanks all night long. I told the maintenance man about it, but he just looks at me like I'm speaking Greek, and he never wipes his shoes before walking on my rugs...
About how long have you been hearing these voices?

Well, let me think... the voices, and this absolute certainty I have that people are watching my archive—all of that has been present for about eight months now. Yes, eight months. I know that because it started right around the time of that terrible ice storm we had late last winter. 

Do you remember that storm? The tree branches outside my building were just coated in it, looking completely encased in glass. I actually tried to photograph them from my living room window, but the glare on the pane was all wrong. I had to open the window to get the shot, and the draft was just freezing! That's when the arthritis really started flaring up again in my knuckles. I ended up buying one of those paraffin wax baths to soak my hands in. Have you ever used one? It feels wonderful, like a warm, heavy glove, but it makes such a terrible mess on the kitchen counter if you aren't careful. I spilled some on a stack of old mail, and it practically sealed my electric bill shut. I had to call the utility company to get my account number, and the woman on the phone had the most grating voice. Not like the whispering women in the walls at all, just very loud and nasal... but yes, about eight months.
During these past eight months, have you had times where you felt unusually energized, elated, or on top of the world?

Oh, absolutely. There are days when I wake up and I just feel... radiant. Truly chosen, you know? Like I have this incredible, pulsing energy for my work. I'll put on my good silk blouse—the emerald green one, it really brings out my eyes. I bought it at a lovely little boutique that used to be on 4th street, right next to a bakery that made the most exquisite almond croissants. They closed down years ago, which is such a shame because you just can't find good almond paste anymore. Everything tastes so synthetic now, don't you think? 

But anyway, I get into these moods where I have this grand plan for the photographs, and I'm moving at lightning speed. But then, if someone questions my plan, or tells me I need to slow down, I become absolutely furious. It's as if they are trying to erase me completely! Like my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she saw me rushing out to the museum with my portfolio recently and had the audacity to tell me to just 'catch my breath.' The nerve! I was so angry. She's always inserting herself where she doesn't belong. Just last week she left a note on my door about my radio being too loud. I was listening to a program about deep-sea diving. Have you ever seen those anglerfish? The ones with the little glowing lanterns on their heads? It's just fascinating how they survive in total darkness down there, carrying their own little light around. I think I'd like to photograph the ocean one day, if I could ever get a waterproof camera.
During these past eight months, have you heard the voices at times when your mood and energy felt completely normal?

Yes, actually. There was a stretch of time... oh, I'd say for several weeks... where I wasn't feeling particularly energized or grand at all. Just my usual self, really. But even then, I still heard the women whispering in the apartment. And I remained absolutely convinced that the arts people were monitoring my phone. 

Speaking of my phone, it's one of those older models, a really lovely mustard yellow color. I found it at an estate sale years ago over in the Heights. The woman who owned the house had the most incredible collection of porcelain teacups. Just rows and rows of them, all hand-painted! I bought one with little purple violets on it, but the handle chipped when I was washing it in the sink. I tried to fix it with that super glue, but I ended up getting it all over my fingers. Have you ever glued your fingers together? It is just terrifying! You feel completely trapped. I had to soak my hands in nail polish remover for nearly an hour, and the smell was just atrocious. It gave me such a dreadful headache that I had to lie down with a cold washcloth over my eyes. It's so hard to find a good, soft washcloth these days, isn't it? They all seem to get so scratchy after just a few times in the laundry, no matter how much fabric softener you use...
